reviews.comment: This class was entertaining. Her lectures are boring for sure and its hard to stay paying attention. The test are all hand written but you get a cheat sheet to use which helps a lot. I think your success in this class also really depends on which TA you get.

reviews.comment:

reviews.comment: She was a thorough lecturer, but your entire grade is determined by like 5 things, two of them being your midterm and final (which the TAs) grade pretty harshly. Lots of reading outside class, but you don't really have to do it tbh
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Solid professor who knows what she is talking about.  She may come off as controversial.
reviews.ratingTags: Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class itself was fine. Do the readings, show up to class, complete the assignments, participate in recitation and you'll get an A. Dr. Radzik's lectures were great, but the class depends more on your TA. Two open-note exams and not that many assignments. Class is discussion-heavy, so attendance is mandatory.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Radzik is a good professor and is very engaging in lectures. Her class is not difficult if you put effort into each assignment and show up to the lecture. Very obtainable A.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed her lectures and her as a professor. This course does require you to put in a lot of effort reading, studying, and writing to succeed, but I found the course worth it as someone interested in law school. The class grade is dependent on only three tests and one final essay, so take that as you will.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class is structured very simple. Go to class, recitation, little HW, work with your TA and you'll get an A. Lectures are interesting but useless. She says to provide reason for excused absences and when I tried to provide her with an explanation and paper work for my illness, she shot down my requesting costing me 2 points off my gradeA- to B+
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The way the course is structured sucks, but her lectures are really interesting. There are a ton of readings and two main papers for the entire course. Not super time consuming but the TA will grade your paper and it can be really rough. The class was fine but to satisfy a credit, there is better options.

The lectures were fine just mainly her going over all of the reading that was provided. The midterm prompt was very vague did not give you much to work with, she seemed as if she was going to grade easy but graded a lot harder and in the instructions nothing was listed of the sort. If you can take someone else do so!
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class itself is very interesting, but that does come with a lot of reading. Dr. Radzik was very accessible outside of class -  don't be afraid to go to office hours, but make sure to go prepared. It will really help you with your grades. This class is by no means a free class, but a good grade is easy if you participate and put in the work.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There are a lot of readings in this course, but no exams. There are weekly group projects, which are pretty easy but she is a very tough grader. You have to write 2 essays in this class and she picks apart every little thing in it, however, you can rewrite one of them for a new grade and she is very accessible outside of class.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Points taken of final grade once you miss more than two classes. Gives very intense feedback, sometimes it is more of an insult than actual feedback. Very nice in class, but a whole different person when it comes to grading/feedback. Reading heavy course. Hard to know exactly what she wants from in in assignments, but going to office hours helps.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Radzik is a very nice person. Attendance is required and you will lose .5 off your entire grade each time you miss class after your 2nd absence. Lots of group work and essay writing. GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS if you want a good grade on your essay. She will tell you everything she wants to change for her to like it. Material is interesting enough.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: In our group assignments, and my individual assignments, the feedback was very passive aggressive. I wont go too deep into specifics but in-class was awesome! I was just made to feel really stupid and it felt belittling at some points in the feedback process. Just my experience. If you decide to take, if you dont show up, you start losing points.

reviews.comment: Way too hard to please, do not take. Everyone who was in that class hated her even though she thought they loved her. The most sweet and adorable person to your face but cold-hearted over email and when it came to grading. I tried to go to office hours for help and she told me I had no idea what I was doing and told me good luck. I had a 79 - C.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Radzik was kind and respectful, encouraged people to share their thoughts and opinions, and her lectures were insightful and interesting. BUT, if you don't complete your work EXACTLY the way she wants it done, you'll be in danger of a B. To get an A I recommend going to office hours and have her look at your work & papers prior to submitting it
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The format may be different from past years because of COVID, but this class was not too bad. Your grade was heavily based on 3 papers and then group activities every week as well as a big project. As long as you pay attention during lectures and do the readings, an A should not be too hard to obtain.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: AWESOME person, excellent professor. Handled COVID-19 better than any other professor I had by far. Easy B, very difficult A. If you want the A, you're going to have to work really hard for it, but regardless, you're going to learn a lot.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Radzik is a great prof, but she will make you work! Granted, this is a writing intensive course, but we've done a LOT of writing (papers, outlines, annotated bibliographies, etc). There's a lot of reading too, but she picks out valuable material and does a great job of explaining it in an engaging way. And she's a very sweet person :)

reviews.comment: the worst prof ive had in 4 years. do NOT take her for the philosophy of law

reviews.comment: **This went from in person to online due to COVID-19** Dr. Radzik delivers clear lectures and is just the sweetest person ever. But when it came to grading, I found her very unfair. "Exercises," which I interpreted being practice, were actually graded rather harshly. Her feedback on paper lacks clarity and her instructions are unclear and confusing
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Radzik has been, by far, my favorite professor at A&M. She is incredibly bright and very kind. The lectures are interesting and I rarely found myself ever looking at the clock. She tries to keep her required books cheap, if not free. She is very easy to contact and gives great feedback. If you're taking a PHIL class should see if she teaches it
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This was my 1st PHIL course, & I'm thankful I got to take it with Dr. Radzik. She is an energetic lecturer, but highly encourages discussion. Only 2 tests, 1 term paper and reading quizzes (tons of reading). I loved the class and the concepts brought up, she also used interesting readings to demonstrate the topics. Go to class, get easy A on exams
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Radzik is incredibly lecture heavy. Be sure to go to class and take thorough notes. As long as you study responsibly for tests, an A is very doable. She is quirky and loves philosophy, and does her best to convey that love to her students. She is very accessible outside of class. There is a lot of reading, A LOT. Only two exams and one paper.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is the best. She is genuinely interested in her students and their education. It was entertaining material and a reasonable amount of class work. She provides the reading, and does not require a textbook. Would definitely recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Radzik is an incredible teacher and human. Ethical theory is the hardest philosophy class I've taken. There is a lot of reading and a lot of concepts. The paper topics seem easy, but she grades hard.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Radzik is very intelligent, although a bit intimidating. She expects you to know the material at the level she has mastered it. Her grading is fair, however her feedback is not. It was rare for a student to be right mid-lecture.

Prof Radzik is amazing. Although you need to attend class in order to participate in discussions she understands if some days you just aren't feeling well and need to miss. She's very approachable and so awesome at helping with writing the essays. 3 essays assigned (two 3-4 page one 7-8 page) and 1 group project. Go to office hours for help w/essay

Class is 95% discussion and 5% lecture. There are readings 2-3 times a week, but they're actually interesting and the discussions in class are fun. Every "test" is an essay, so be ready to write. I found all essays to be easy, but some of the class struggled. If you don't mind reading & are an above average writer, the class will be a breeze.

Dr. Radzik's class is tough, but manageable. Grades consist of 3 essays, one of which is 10 pages long, and occasional pop quizzes over the readings that were all pretty easy. Class is mostly discussion-based and the lectures are very interesting. She's a pretty tough grader, but she's also very willing to help you out. Overall, she's a great prof.

shes a great teacher, i learned alot but i had to study hard.  If you go to class and take notes, you never need the textbook.  If you don't go, you can just read the textbook.  Alot depends on your TA though.
3 papers...weekly quizes..open book final exam.. pretty easy class..

Be prepared to take weekly online quizzes that are only 4 questions long (miss 1 = 75) that are worth 15% of your grade. This along with writing papers that will be ruthlessly graded by egotistical grad students out to prove they know more than you do about asking the question, why?.
